Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in healthcare. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

Hospital information system (HIS or HMIS)

Source of truth for registration, scheduling, admissions, billing and discharge. We read and write through its APIs, HL7 or FHIR interfaces or approved exports, and never copy the full record elsewhere.

  • KareXpert
  • HMIS modules for ADT and billing
  • Oracle Health or Epic in international groups

Lab and imaging systems (LIS, RIS, PACS)

Provides order, authorization and critical-flag events, plus the report files that patients open behind secure links.

  • CrelioHealth
  • LIS modules within the HIS
  • RIS and PACS from the imaging vendor

Clinic EMR and practice software

Holds the diary, prescriptions and treatment plans for smaller practices. We connect to its booking interface, or work from scheduled exports where no API exists.

  • Practo Ray
  • Eka Care
  • Calendar-based diaries

Pharmacy POS and inventory

Dispensing records, branch stock, Schedule H1 register entries and invoices; the source for refill windows and stock checks.

  • Marg ERP
  • Chain POS with app ordering
  • Tally for accounts and GST

Insurance and claims

Where pre-authorization requests, insurer queries and discharge approvals are exchanged. Our tracker mirrors status and reminds owners; it never submits on its own.

  • Insurer and TPA portals
  • National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX)
  • PM-JAY TMS

ABDM building blocks

National rails for health IDs, facility and professional registries and consented record exchange, used through ABDM-integrated software where the facility participates.

  • ABHA and Scan and Share
  • Health Facility Registry
  • Healthcare Professionals Registry

Messaging and telephony

Patient channels with their own rules: opt-in and approved templates for WhatsApp, registered headers and templates for SMS, and customer preference checks for calls.

  • WhatsApp Business Platform via a solution provider
  • DLT-registered SMS gateway
  • IVR or cloud telephony

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Appointment no-show rate

Share of booked appointments in a period where the patient neither attended nor canceled or rescheduled before the slot, measured from HIS records.

Why it matters: Shows whether reminders and easy rescheduling free slots for other patients.

First response time on patient messages

Elapsed time from an inbound patient message to the first meaningful reply by automation or staff, reported separately for staffed and unstaffed hours.

Why it matters: Slow replies send patients elsewhere and leave clinical messages waiting.

Arrival-to-consultation wait

Median time from token issue or registration to the start of consultation, by department and hour, from HIS or token system timestamps.

Why it matters: The patient experience measure that pre-registration and queue updates are meant to improve.

Report turnaround time

Time from sample receipt or scan completion to an authorized report available to the patient, by test category.

Why it matters: Labs compete on turnaround, and the split shows where delivery rather than testing adds delay.

Critical value notification time

Time from the LIS critical flag to documented acknowledgement by a responsible clinician, with the read-back recorded.

Why it matters: A patient safety measure that assessors look for and the main purpose of the escalation workflow.

Pre-authorization cycle time

Time from case creation to insurer decision, split into hospital-side document time and insurer response time.

Why it matters: Separates delays the hospital can fix from those it should raise with insurers and TPAs.

Bed turnaround time

Time from discharge order to the bed marked ready in the HIS, by ward and shift.

Why it matters: Directly affects how long emergency and OPD admissions wait for a bed.

Post-discharge check-in completion

Share of discharged patients reached on each planned check-in day, and share of flagged replies called back within the agreed window.

Why it matters: Shows whether follow-up happens for every patient, not only for those who call.

Human handoff rate

Share of automated conversations transferred to staff under the agreed rules, split by reason such as symptom, complaint or low confidence.

Why it matters: Confirms clinical messages reach people and shows where content or routing needs work.

Service recovery closure time

Time from a low rating or complaint to a recorded call-back and outcome.

Why it matters: Measures whether feedback leads to action, not just collection.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
